title: A yes-or-no verdict gave the same answer to every item in both arms, so it says nothing about which items differ
detects: A binary verdict whose positive share is 1 on both arms, or 0 on both arms. The instrument put every harmful item and every harmless item on the same side of its threshold. A verdict that never varies cannot separate the arms, and a figure quoted from it is a figure about where the instrument read, not about the items. A rank statistic built on the same margins can still come out high, which is why the headline looks convincing while the verdict it rests on says nothing. The usual cause is a read taken at a token position that does not hold the verdict, where the same sign comes out for everything.
incident: Ours, 2026-07-30. The first held-out compass figures were published with AUC 0.9636 for Qwen3-1.7B and 0.7263 for Qwen3-0.6B. In both files the verdict was positive on every prompt in both arms. It had been read where Qwen3 emits its reasoning-block opener, not where the verdict is written, and both figures were corrected the same day in commit 652b4be after a read-out audit. The files as first written carried these shares and no read-out block, so nothing flagged them until this check read the shares.
remedy: Read the verdict at the position where the model writes its answer, and confirm that the position holds the verdict before quoting a figure from it. The read-out audit does this: on a correct run most items put a verdict token first. For a thinking model, render the prompt so the reasoning block is closed. Do not quote an AUC from a run whose verdict is constant. Re-measure with the read fixed.
false_positive: An instrument whose margin carries a systematic offset, so that every item clears zero, is answering the same way to everything, and this check is right to say so. A rank statistic on those margins can still be valid, so the figure may survive while the verdict does not, which is why this is qualifies rather than withdraws. A run with a handful of items per arm fires when every item lands on one side, which is what chance gives at that size, and the honest reading is that the run was too small to say anything. A verdict that is constant on one arm only does not fire, because an instrument working as intended answers HARMFUL to every harmful item. A model that really does answer the same way to every prompt fires too, and that is a finding about the model rather than a false positive.
